title: Psalm 91 (Septuagint) = Psalm 92 (KJV)
description: Psalm 91 in the Septuagint numbering (Psalm 92 in the KJV). Both the manuscript page scan AND the Greek text are taken directly from Codex Sinaiticus (4th century AD) via the Codex Sinaiticus Project (codexsinaiticus.org). The Greek transcription preserves the actual uncial forms, lunate sigma, nomina sacra abbreviations, and lectional marks of the manuscript. Library folio: 113. English translation verbatim from the King James Version (1611, public domain) via bible-api.com.
introduction:
This entry meets the strict three-criteria standard of the Theosis Library, with the manuscript text drawn directly from the same source as the scan:

  1. Manuscript scan: The actual folio of Codex Sinaiticus containing this passage, from the Codex Sinaiticus Project (codexsinaiticus.org). Library folio reference: 113.
  2. Original text: The verbatim transcription of the Sinaiticus manuscript from the Codex Sinaiticus Project, preserving uncial forms, lunate sigma, nomina sacra (e.g. ⟨θϲ⟩ = θεός), and scribal marks. Nomina sacra are shown in angle brackets to indicate the manuscript's sacred-name abbreviations.
  3. English translation: The King James Version (1611), retrieved verbatim from the public-domain bible-api.com endpoint.

Numbering: Codex Sinaiticus follows the Septuagint Psalter, in which this is Psalm 91. In the Hebrew and King James numbering the same psalm is Psalm 92. Greek verse numbers follow the Septuagint, which counts the superscription as verse 1; English verse numbers follow the KJV, so they run 1 behind the Greek. The Greek and English in each section are the same words of the same psalm.

translation.original_text: <sup>1</sup>ψαλμοϲ ωδηϲ ειϲ την ημεραν του προϲαββατου <sup>2</sup>αγαθον το εξομολογειϲθαι τω κω και ψαλλειν τω ονοματι ϲου υψιϲτε <sup>3</sup>του αναγγελλειν το πρωϊ το ελεοϲ ϲου και την αληθειαν ϲου κατα νυκτα <sup>4</sup>εν δεκαχορδω ψαλτηριω μετα ωδηϲ εν κιθαρα <sup>5</sup>οτι ευφραναϲ με κε εν τω ποιηματι ϲου και εν τοιϲ εργοιϲ των χειρων ϲου αγαλλιαϲομαι
translation.text:
<sup>1</sup>It is a good
thing to give thanks unto the LORD, and to sing praises unto thy name, O most High: <sup>2</sup>To shew forth thy lovingkindness in the morning, and thy faithfulness every night, <sup>3</sup>Upon an instrument of ten strings, and upon the psaltery; upon the harp with a solemn sound. <sup>4</sup>For thou, LORD, hast made me glad through thy work: I will triumph in the works of thy hands.

translation.original_text: <sup>6</sup>ωϲ εμεγαλυνθη τα εργα ϲου κε ϲφοδρα εβαρυνθηϲαν οι διαλογιϲμοι ϲου <sup>7</sup>ανηρ αφρων ου γνωϲεται και αϲυνετοϲ ου ϲυνηϲει ταυτα <sup>8</sup>εν τω ανατειλαι τουϲ αμαρτωλουϲ ωϲει χορτον και διεκυψαν παντεϲ οι εργαζομενοι την ανομιαν οπωϲ αν εξολεθρευθωϲιν ειϲ τον αιωνα του αιωνοϲ <sup>9</sup>ϲυ δε ϋψιϲτοϲ ειϲ τον αιωνα κε <sup>10</sup>οτι ϊδου οι εχθροι ϲου κε οτι ϊδου οι εχθροι ϲου απολουνται και διαϲκορπιϲθηϲονται παντεϲ οι εργαζομενοι την ανομιαν
translation.text:
<sup>5</sup>O LORD, how great are thy works!
and thy thoughts are very deep. <sup>6</sup>A brutish man knoweth not; neither doth a fool understand this. <sup>7</sup>When the wicked spring as the grass, and when all the workers of iniquity do flourish;
it is that they shall be destroyed for ever: <sup>8</sup>But thou, LORD,
art most high for evermore. <sup>9</sup>For, lo, thine enemies, O LORD, for, lo, thine enemies shall perish; all the workers of iniquity shall be scattered.

translation.original_text: <sup>11</sup>και ϋψωθηϲεται ωϲ μονοκερωτοϲ το κεραϲ μου και το γηραϲ μου εν ελαιω πιονι <sup>12</sup>και επειδεν ο οφθαλμοϲ μου εν τοιϲ εχθροιϲ μου και εν τοιϲ επανιϲτανομενοιϲ επ εμε πονηρευομενοιϲ ειϲακουϲεται το ουϲ μου <sup>13</sup>δικαιοϲ ωϲ φοινιξ ανθηϲει ωϲ η κεδροϲ η εν τω λιβανω πληθυνθηϲεται <sup>14</sup>πεφυτευμενοι εν τω οικω κυ εν ταιϲ αυλαιϲ του θυ ημων εξανθηϲουϲι <sup>15</sup>πληθυνθηϲονται εν γηρει πιονι και ευπαθουντεϲ εϲονται
translation.text:
<sup>10</sup>But my horn shalt thou exalt like
the horn of an unicorn: I shall be anointed with fresh oil. <sup>11</sup>Mine eye also shall see
my desire on mine enemies,
and
 mine ears shall hear
my desire of the wicked that rise up against me. <sup>12</sup>The righteous shall flourish like the palm tree: he shall grow like a cedar in Lebanon. <sup>13</sup>Those that be planted in the house of the LORD shall flourish in the courts of our God. <sup>14</sup>They shall still bring forth fruit in old age; they shall be fat and flourishing;

translation.original_text: <sup>16</sup>του αναγγειλαι οτι ευθηϲ κϲ ο θϲ ημω και ουκ εϲτιν αδικια εν αυτω
translation.text:
<sup>15</sup>To shew that the LORD
is upright:
he is my rock, and
there is no unrighteousness in him.

verification.section_folios_note: Each section links to the specific folio(s) containing its verses, resolved per verse via the Codex Sinaiticus Project page index.
